Dataset containing all data that **BMW AG** is providing towards www.dataforroadsafety.eu 

Each event is generated out of respective vehicle signals in a completely anonymized way. The data format is www.sensoris.org V1.6.0 

The feed contains data from various vehicle generations comprising several million actively contributing vehicles in Europe . 
All location information in the field dataMessage.eventGroup.localizationCategory.vehiclePositionAndOrientation is a list of 3 vehiclePositions in ascending order (from oldest to youngest), the one in the middle is closest to the timestamp, the first and third one are the vehiclePositions right before and after this one, unless the timestamp is less than one second - then the next ones are taken. 
dataMessage.eventGroup.localizationCategory.vehiclePositionAndOrientation.timestamp.posixTime (Int64Value) is rounded to the nearest 5 minute interval, and only set for one vehicle position: the one closest to the timestamp, 
dataMessage.eventGroup.localizationCategory.vehiclePositionAndOrientation.positionAndAccuracy.geographicWgs84.longitude (Int64Value) is restricted to -180 to 180, scaled to 10**8 
dataMessage.eventGroup.localizationCategory.vehiclePositionAndOrientation.positionAndAccuracy.geographicWgs84.latitude (Int64Value) is restricted to -90 to 90, scaled to 10**8 
dataMessage.eventGroup.localizationCategory.vehiclePositionAndOrientation.orientationAndAccuracy.eulerVehicle.yaw (Int64Value) is restricted to 0 to 360, scaled to 10**2, can be null, north is 0, east is 90 
dataMessage.eventGroup.trafficEventsCategory.hazard.envelope.timestamp.posixTime (Int64Value) is rounded to the closest even 5 min multiple in the past (consumers are advised to use their reception time to get a more precise generation time) 
dataMessage.eventGroup.trafficEventsCategory.hazard.envelope.detectionType.type (enum) is set to various values according to the usecase, indicating the algorithmic logic applied in generating the event according to the SENSORIS specification 
dataMessage.eventGroup.trafficEventsCategory.hazard.typeAndConfidence.type (enum) is set to various values according to the usecases. The mapping to the usecases described in delegated regulation 886/2013, which is the base for www.dataforroadsafety.eu, is: 
SRTI category | BMW Usecase Temporary slippery road | SLIPPERY_ROAD Animal, people, obstacles, debris on the road | BROKEN_DOWN_VEHICLE, ACCIDENT (meaning the ego-vehicle) Unprotected accident area | BROKEN_DOWN_VEHICLE, ACCIDENT Unmanaged blockage of a road | BROKEN_DOWN_VEHICLE, ACCIDENT (meaning the ego-vehicle) Wrong-way driver | WRONG_WAY_VEHICLE (meaning the ego vehicle) 

The weather type usecases are encoded in dataMessage.eventGroup.visibilitycondition.typeandconfidence.type 
SRTI category | BMW Usecase Reduced visibility | LOW_HEAVY_RAIN, LOW_FOG Exceptional weather conditions | LOW_HEAVY_RAIN, LOW_FOG SRTI category 'Short-term road works' is currently not implemented

Dataset for the **'Accident'** provided by **BMW AG**.

Each event is generated out of respective vehicle signals (e.g. Emergency-Call trigger) in a completely anonymized way. The position information given consists of up to three consecutive points sorted by time, only one point has a timestamp, that is rounded to 5 minutes.

The events are provided for the geographic rectangle given by **northLatitude** = 71.5, **southLatitude** = 34.5, **eastLongitude** = 65.0, **westLongitude** = -11.0 .

The dataset contains events of the last 30 minutes and gets updated every 5 minutes.

Please note that the datasets are deactivated between von 7 pm - 6 am CEST and during the weekend.

dataOffers.descriptionShortText:
# What is Origin-Destination Data?

## Description

Origin-Destination Data provides insights into the start and end location of individual vehicle trips.

---

## Data Source

The data is sourced from millions of vehicles globally via vetted partners, including:

- **Automotive OEMs**:  
  Vehicles with embedded connectivity from the car manufacturer.

- **Fleets with after-sales telematics devices**:  
  In-vehicle hardware installed post-manufacturing.

---

## Use Cases

- **Transportation analytics**:  
  Used by traffic consultants, road operators, municipalities, and SaaS analytics platforms to analyze road usage, people movement, and perform targeted before-and-after assessments of infrastructure or signage changes.

- **Emission analysis**:  
  Enables stakeholders to estimate emissions based on traffic information.

---

## Origin-Destination Data Schema

**Main Attributes**

- **`trip_id`** (string):  
  Hashed ID for a single trip.

- **`start_time`** (string):  
  Time when the trip started (datetime UTC / seconds) in ISO 8601 format.

- **`end_time`** (string):  
  Time when the trip ended (datetime UTC / seconds) in ISO 8601 format.

- **`duration`** (integer):  
  Duration of the trip in seconds.

- **`start_point`** (string):  
  H3 hash of the trip’s starting location at H3 resolution 11.

- **`start_latitude`** (double):  
  Latitude of the center of the H3 grid at the trip start point.

- **`start_longitude`** (double):  
  Longitude of the center of the H3 grid at the trip start point.

- **`end_point`** (string):  
  H3 hash of the trip’s ending location at H3 resolution 11.

- **`end_latitude`** (double):  
  Latitude of the center of the H3 grid at the trip end point.

- **`end_longitude`** (double):  
  Longitude of the center of the H3 grid at the trip end point.

- **`distance`** (double):  
  Total distance covered during the trip in meters.

- **`avg_speed`** (double):  
  Average vehicle speed during the trip in km/h.

- **`vehicle_type`** (string):  
  Vehicle category (passenger, light van, heavy truck, bus, other).

- **`fuel_type`** (string):  
  Fuel type used by the vehicle.

---

## Origin-Destination Data Specs

### Historicity

Historical data is available as of 2024. Availability differs by country.

---

### Trip Types

The dataset can include any of the following trip types:

- All trips within a selected geographical area  
- Trips that start within a selected area  
- Trips that end within a selected area

---

### Vehicle Types

The following vehicle types are available in the datasets (availability varies by country):

- **Passenger car**

- **Light commercial vehicle (LCV)**  
  These are van-type vehicles.  
  Examples include: Renault Master, Renault Trafic, Mercedes-Benz Sprinter, Peugeot B**o**xer, V**o**lkswagen Crafter, Fiat Ducato, Opel Crossland, Citroën Berlingo

- **Heavy truck**  
  Vehicles with a gross weight above three and a half tonnes.

- **Bus**

- **Other**  
  Unclassified vehicle types.

---

## Data Anonymisation

Data anonymisation techniques are applied to ensure privacy. Key features include:

- **No exact locations**:  
  Instead of precise coordinates, Mobito uses the **[H3 hexagonal grid system](https://h3geo.org/)** to generalize locations.

- **[H3 Resolution 11 precision](https://h3geo.org/docs/core-library/restable/#average-area-in-m2)**:  
  Each location is mapped to a hexagonal area to ensure privacy while preserving analytical value.

dataOffers.descriptionShortText:
# What is Standstill Events Data?

## Description

Standstill Events Data provides insights into where and for how long vehicles remain stationary. This data helps analyze stop locations and durations, offering valuable context for traffic and mobility trends.

---

## Data Source

The data is sourced from millions of vehicles globally via vetted partners, including:

- **Automotive OEMs**:  
  Vehicles with embedded connectivity from the car manufacturer.

- **Fleets with after-sales telematics devices**:  
  In-vehicle hardware installed post-manufacturing.

---

## Use Cases

Standstill Events Data becomes even more powerful when combined with Probe Data, allowing for a deeper understanding of trip patterns, traffic volumes, and stop durations. Key applications include:

- **Site selection**:  
  Identify optimal locations for retail store expansions and EV charging station deployments based on vehicle stop frequency and dwell times.

- **Route planning**:  
  Companies with large vehicle fleets (e.g., transportation companies) use this data to optimise routes, reduce fuel consumption, and improve operational efficiency.

- **Transportation analytics**:  
  Used by traffic consultants, road operators, municipalities, and SaaS analytics platforms to analyze road safety, road usage, and people movement. Also supports before-and-after studies to assess infrastructure and signage changes.

---

## Standstill Events Data Schema

**Main Attributes**

- **`start_time`** (string):  
  The time when the standstill event started (datetime UTC / seconds).

- **`end_time`** (string):  
  The time when the standstill event ended (datetime UTC / seconds).

- **`h3`** (string):  
  H3 hash of the standstill event location in H3 resolution 11.

- **`latitude`** (double):  
  Latitude of the center of the H3 grid.

- **`longitude`** (double):  
  Longitude of the center of the H3 grid.

- **`duration`** (double):  
  Full duration of the standstill event in seconds.

- **`fuel_type`** (string):  
  Fuel type used by the vehicle.

- **`vehicle_type`** (string):  
  Vehicle category (passenger, light van, heavy truck, bus, other).

---

## Standstill Events Data Specs

### Historicity

Historical data is available as of 2025

---

### Geographical Granularity

Data can be delivered at the following levels:

- Custom polygon area  
- Specific road segment

---

### Vehicle Types

The following vehicle types are available in the datasets (availability varies per country):

- **Passenger car**

- **Light commercial vehicle (LCV)**  
  These are van-type vehicles.  
  Examples include: Renault Master, Renault Trafic, Mercedes-Benz Sprinter, Peugeot B**o**xer, V**o**lkswagen Crafter, Fiat Ducato, Opel Crossland, Citroën Berlingo

- **Heavy truck**  
  Vehicles with a gross weight above three and a half tonnes.

- **B us**

- **Miscellaneous**  
  Unclassified vehicle types.

---

## Data Anonymisation

Data anonymisation techniques are applied to ensure privacy. Key features include:

- **No exact locations**:  
  Instead of precise coordinates, Mobito uses the **[H3 hexagonal grid system](https://h3geo.org/)** to generalize locations.

- **[H3 Resolution 11 precision](https://h3geo.org/docs/core-library/restable/#average-area-in-m2)**:  
  Each location is mapped to a hexagonal area to ensure privacy while preserving analytical value.

# What is Driving Events Data?

## Description

The Mobito Driving Events Data provides anonymized insights into harsh driving behaviors, including harsh braking, acceleration/deceleration, sharp cornering (left/right), and crash events.

---

## Data Source

The data is sourced from millions of vehicles globally via vetted partners, including:

- **Automotive OEMs**:  
  Vehicles with embedded connectivity from the car manufacturer.

- **Fleets with after-sales telematics devices**:  
  In-vehicle hardware installed post-manufacturing.

---

## Driving Event Types

Common event types used to characterize driving behavior include:

- Braking  
- Cornering (left/right)  
- Speeding up / acceleration  
- Crash (while driving or parked)

---

## Use Cases

Mobito’s driving event data enables road safety analysis, infrastructure planning, and driver behavior profiling.

- **Road safety**:  
  Identify high-risk road segments based on driving behavior and near-miss incidents. Supports better maintenance planning and prioritization.

- **Road infrastructure**:  
  Assess and plan the impact of infrastructure improvements on traffic flow and safety.

- **Driving behavior analysis**:  
  Help automotive engineers develop driver personas to inform the design of next-generation vehicles.

---

## Driving Events Data Schema

**Main Attributes**

- **`unique_id`** (string):  
  Hashed ID for a vehicle that rotates every few minutes, up to a maximum of 24 hours.

- **`start_time`** (string):  
  Timestamp at the start of the event (UTC, ISO 8601 format).

- **`end_time`** (string):  
  Timestamp at the end of the event (UTC, ISO 8601 format).

- **`latitude`** (double):  
  Latitude position at the start of the event (±10 m accuracy).

- **`longitude`** (double):  
  Longitude position at the start of the event (±10 m accuracy).

- **`start_speed`** (integer):  
  Vehicle speed at the start of the event.

- **`end_speed`** (integer):  
  Vehicle speed at the end of the event.

- **`acceleration_direction`** (integer):  
  Direction of acceleration in degrees.

- **`vehicle_type`** (string):  
  Vehicle category (passenger, light van, heavy truck, bus, other).

- **`event_type`** (string):  
  Type of event (e.g., cornering_left, cornering_right, brake, speedup, crash_driving, crash_parked).

---

## Data Sample

A small sample is available at the link below, which helps illustrate the data schema.

**[MOBITO Anonymized Driving Events Data Sample Schema](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1KES9cwuoAoLQ3TCethAhWHJDt4RTK2-L-BhskoYLE0M/edit?usp=sharing)**

---

## Driving Events Data Specs

### Historicity

Historical data is available starting from November 2024. Availability varies by country.

---

### Geographical Granularity

Data can be delivered at the following levels:

- Country  
- State / Province  
- City  
- Custom polygon area  
- Specific road segment

---

### Vehicle Types

The following vehicle types are included in the datasets (availability varies by country):

- **Passenger car**

- **Light commercial vehicle (LCV)**  
  These are van-type vehicles.  
  Examples include: Renault Master, Renault Trafic, Mercedes-Benz Sprinter, Peugeot B**o**xer, V**o**lkswagen Crafter, Fiat Ducato, Opel Crossland, Citroën Berlingo

- **Heavy truck**  
  Vehicles with a gross weight above three and a half tonnes.

- **B us**

- **Miscellaneous**  
  Unclassified vehicle types.

---

## Car Brands and Models

MOBITO offers multi-brand vehicle data. However, vehicle make and model details are only available for a limited portion of the total car park.

dataOffers.descriptionShortText:
# What is Probe Data?

## Description
**Probe data**, or **Floating Car data** as it is often referred to, is anonymized, timestamped, trajectory-level vehicle location data.

---

## Data Source

The data is sourced by millions of vehicles globally from our vetted partners including:

- **Automotive OEMs**: Vehicles with embedded connectivity from the car manufacturer  
- **Fleets**: Vehicles with after-sales in-vehicle hardware telematics devices

---

## Use Cases

- **Traffic management**  
  Our data fuels dynamic traffic light systems, incident response management, and other ITS applications (Intelligent Transport Systems).

- **Transportation analytics**  
  Traffic consultants, road operators, municipalities, and SaaS analytics platforms use our data to understand road safety, road usage, people movement, and perform targeted before & after analytics to assess infrastructure and signage changes.

- **Site-selection**  
  Our data supports models that assess the best location for new retail store openings and EV charging station rollouts, based on footfall and cannibalization estimates.

- **Event Planning**  
  Organizers of concerts, sports, and similar events can analyze traffic patterns to optimize event start/end times and manage traffic in real-time.

- **Route Planning**  
  Companies with large vehicle fleets (e.g., delivery, taxi, or transportation companies) use this data to optimize routes, reduce fuel consumption, and improve operational efficiency.

- **Emission Analysis**  
  Stakeholders can estimate emission hotspots based on traffic information.

---

## Probe Data Schema

**Main Attributes**

- **`unique_id` or `trip_id`** (string):  
  Hashed ID for a vehicle (rotating every few minutes up to a maximum of 24 hours), or hashed ID for a single trip.

- **`timestamp`** (string):  
  Date & time of the record (in UTC, ISO 8601 format).

- **`latitude`** (double):  
  Latitude position of the vehicle (±10m accuracy).

- **`longitude`** (double):  
  Longitude position of the vehicle (±10m accuracy).

- **`speed`** (double):  
  Speed of the vehicle in km/h.

- **`heading`** (double):  
  Direction of the vehicle in degrees (0–359, where 0 = North, 90 = East).

- **`vehicle_type`** (string):  
  Vehicle category (e.g., passenger, light van, heavy truck, bus, other).

---

### Extended Probe Data – Additional Attributes

Additional attributes might be available depending on the geography of interest. These attributes are offered at an additional cost.

**Indicative list:**
- Acceleration in X, Y, Z axis  
- Fuel level  
- Electrical consumption  
- Wiper state  
- Fog lights  
- ESP  
- Air temperature  
- Fuel type  
- Vehicle make & model  
- Vehicle weight  
- Road type and speed limit

---

## Data Sample

A small sample is available at the link below for download, which can help you better understand the data schema.

**[MOBITO Anonymized Probe Vehicle Data Sample Schema](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1GBsILsEzrijtmaVa3KVvxW4AXNMCd02PRNPj2K3ezUM/edit?usp=sharing)**

---

## Probe Data Specs

### Capturing Frequency

Capturing frequency differs depending on the data source and the geography.  
It ranges from **3 seconds up to a minute**.

**Indicative list:**

- **Italy**:  
  Average frequency – 3 seconds

- **Germany**:  
  Average frequency – 10 seconds

- **France**:  
  Average frequency – 10 seconds

- **Netherlands**:  
  Average frequency – 10 seconds

- **United Kingdom**:  
  Average frequency – 10 seconds

- **Spain**:  
  Average frequency – 10 seconds

> Note: Long-distance uninterrupted travel on highways might reduce the capturing frequency.

---

### Geographical Granularity

Data can be delivered at the following geographical levels:

- Country  
- State/Province  
- City  
- Custom polygon area  
- Specific road segment

---

More details can be found here: **[MOBITO Anonymized Probe Vehicle Data](https://support.mobito.io/en/articles/10638625-probe-data-product)**

# Pedestrian Footfall Dataset

## Details

We offer a comprehensive pedestrian footfall dataset, collected with high-precision people-counting sensors and cameras. This dataset captures the flow of pedestrian traffic across diverse environments.

The footfall data is derived from multiple sources, ensuring high accuracy and representativeness:

- **Smart Sensors**: High-resolution people-counting devices installed at strategic entry and exit points.  
- **Cameras with AI-based Analytics**: Video streams processed with computer vision to detect and count individuals without compromising privacy.  
- **Event-based Sampling**: Temporary deployments during festivals, cultural events, and seasonal tourism peaks.  

## Availability

The pedestrian dataset can be provided on a use case basis, depending on demand. Available cases include:  

- Historic districts of major cities  
- Shopping malls and commercial hubs  
- Seasonal tourist hotspots such as beaches  
- Cultural centers, museums, and exhibition venues  
- Large-scale public events and festivals  
- Others: just ask if you are interested 

## Technical details

The dataset contains:  

- **Coordinates**: Latitude and longitude of counting points  
- **Footfall Counts**: Integer values representing the number of people
- **Timestamps**: CEST-based time series for historical analysis. Data granularity can range from 15 minutes to daily.
- **Format**: CSV, Excel or JSON via API access  

## Commercial details

This dataset is commercially licensed. The following process applies for obtaining the data:  

1. Bilateral negotiation of contract terms with Dinycon SIstemas S.L.  
2. After successful agreement, activation of your connector for the requested use case.  
3. Access to the purchased dataset via secure API or file transfer.  

For inquiries or dataset access, please contact **pablo.cp@dinycon.com**

# Hazard score dataset for the road network

## Description 

We offer a comprehensive "hazard score" dataset for the road network. This score evaluates the risk level for each road segment on a scale from 1 to 5, with 1 indicating lower risk and 5 indicating very high risk. The hazard score is calculated with a high level of geographical accuracy with road segments or nods being 10m or less.. Our data is designed to assist in risk assessment, road safety analysis, and urban planning. The dataset is provided in GeoJSON format, making it easy to integrate with various geographic information systems.

The hazard score is derived from multiple data sources, ensuring a robust and accurate risk assessment:

- Accident Data: Historical records of traffic accidents.
- User Reports: Real-time reports and feedback from users.
- Vehicle Pulse Data: Sensor data from vehicles indicating road conditions and incidents.

## Availability

The hazard score is offered on a regional basis for the desired areas. Cities, federal states, Germany-wide. 

Additional information, such as detailed accident data, user hazard reports and much more can optionally be provided as structured data.

---

## Technical details

The data set contains:

- Coordinates: Latitude and Longitude
- Score: Integer value ranging from 1 to 5, where: 1 = Lower risk, 5 = Very high risk
- Format: GeoJSON

Access to the nationwide timetable information system via the EFA JSON API.

An example request could look like this:

https://www.efa-bw.de/mobidata-bw/XML_STOPFINDER_REQUEST?outputFormat=rapidJSON&type_sf=any&name_sf=de:08111:6115


The stop Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof is queried here with the information that the stop type can be any. Unlike TRIAS, the query parameters are included in the URL and not determined in the body with the same URL.

The TRIAS terms of use apply to the use of the EFA JSON API; you can take note of these in advance.

dataOffers.descriptionShortText:
# Datensatz-Spezifikation: PidMo
**Parkhäuser im Datenraum Mobilität**

Dieser Datensatz enthält die technische Spezifikation des im Forschungsprojekt **PidMo** entwickelten Datenmodells. Das primäre Ziel ist es, die technologische Isolation von Parkhaus-Infrastrukturen aufzubrechen und eine souveräne sowie interoperable Einbindung in nationale Mobilitätsdatenräume (**Mobility Data Space (MDS)** und **Mobilithek**) zu ermöglichen.

---

### 🛠 Kerninhalte und Struktur

* **Standardisierung:** Die Modellierung basiert auf dem europäischen Standard **DATEX II (CEN/TS 16157)**. Es wurden spezifische Profile entwickelt, die exakt auf moderne Mobilitätsszenarien zugeschnitten sind.
* **Differenzierung der Datenarten:** Das Modell unterscheidet systematisch zwischen:
    * **Statischen Stammdaten:** z. B. Standorte, Kapazitäten oder Zertifizierungen für Landeflächen.
    * **Dynamischen Prozessdaten:** z. B. Echtzeit-Belegungsraten oder automatisierte Buchungsvorgänge.

---

### 🌐 Domänenspezifische Erweiterungen (Use-Cases)

Das Modell beinhaltet spezialisierte Attribute und Funktionen für vier zentrale Anwendungsfelder:

1.  **Automated Valet Parking (AVP Typ 2):** Infrastrukturbasierte Unterstützung für vollautomatisierte, fahrerlose Parkvorgänge.
2.  **Intermodale Shuttle-Anbindung:** Synchronisation von autonomen Shuttlesystemen mit dem Individualverkehr.
3.  **Urban Air Mobility (UAM):** Qualifizierung von Parkhausdächern als Start- und Landeplätze für Flugdrohnen (**Vertiports**).
4.  **Urban Hubs:** Integration von Logistikflächen zur Optimierung des städtischen Warenumschlags.

---

### 🚀 Technischer & Strategischer Nutzen

* **Plattformfähigkeit:** Das Datenset ermöglicht es Betreibern, ihre Infrastruktur als aktive **Mobility Hubs** in das urbane Verkehrsnetz zu integrieren.
* **Implementierung:** Durch die Bereitstellung als **UML-Spezifikation** und **XML-Schema** wird eine direkte technische Umsetzung für Software-Entwickler und Systemintegratoren ermöglicht.

---

### 📂 Download & Zugriff

Das vollständige Datenmodell inklusive aller Spezifikationen steht unter folgendem Link zur Verfügung:

> **[Zum Datensatz auf Zenodo: 18890553](https://zenodo.org/records/18890553)**

# Osnabrück Traffic Sensor Dataset

The dataset contains timeseries data from 66 **Traffic Eye Universal (TEU)** traffic sensors measuring traffic count and speed. The sensors are located as pairs on streets of the city of Osnabrück. One sensor of a pair measures into one traffic direction and the second sensor in the opposite direction. Traffic is categorized into car, truck, truck_with_trailer, and unclassified. The data is provided raw without preprocessing.

## Timeframe

- **Startdate:** 03.01.2022
- **Enddate:** 09.11.2023
- **Timeresolution:** 5 Min
- **Theorethical number of samples per timeseries/sensor:** 194,400

Their expertise, insights, discussions, and commitment are invaluable. Especially, we want to thank the municipality of Osnabrück for providing the static and dynamic raw traffic data.

This work is part of the *Intelligenter Intermodaler Pendlerverkehr* project, also known as *Intelligent Pendeln*. Intelligent Pendeln has received funding from the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) program “[Forschungsnetzwerk Anonymisierung für eine sichere Datennutzung](https://www.forschungsnetzwerk-anonymisierung.de/index.php/tagungsband-2025)” under grant agreement No 16KISA120.

Some computation of this research was carried out using computing resources of the High Performance Computing (HPC) cluster of the Osnabrück University of Applied Sciences, which were provided by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) within the [HiPer4All@HSOS](https://www.hs-osnabrueck.de/hpc-cluster/) project.
